pool.text: The British South African Company took formal control of the region around Lusaka.
Lusaka was founded as a water stop along the northbound railway route.
Several stores and a hotel opened, persuading the BSAC to declare Lusaka a recognised town.
The British imperial government took direct control of Northern Rhodesia through a governor and legislative council.
The British colonial administration decided to move its capital from Livingstone to Lusaka.
The legislative council approved the report confirming Lusaka as the planned capital.
Lusaka formally became the capital with a week-long celebration.
The UK launched an investigation into a possible merger of Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland.
The government passed the African Housing Ordinance authorizing permanent residential suburbs for Africans.
A development plan for Lusaka gained statutory approval for the first time.
The British government approved the plan to merge Northern Rhodesia with its two neighbors into a federation.
Northern Rhodesia became independent as the Republic of Zambia with Lusaka named as its capital.
Lusaka formed a twinning relationship with Dushanbe in Tajikistan.
Lusaka established a twinning agreement with Los Angeles in the United States.
The city hosted the Fifth Summit Conference of East and Central African States.
The Lusaka Stock Exchange was launched in the city.
An urban and regional planning bill was enacted by the government.
The 58-metre-high Tower was launched by Sun Share Ltd.
The city council began a programme of road improvements to tackle chronic traffic congestion.
A synagogue hosted by the Chabad of Zambia opened in the city.
